# About This Book {.unnumbered}

This book grew from courses in *Behavioral Economics* and *Decision, Persuasion, and Negotiation* taught and refined over several years. Its central question is practical: how can people make better decisions when attention is limited, the future is uncertain, and other people have goals of their own? The chapters follow that question from individual judgment to conversations, agreements, and institutions.

The book’s recurring ethical test is whether a message, environment, conversation, agreement, or decision system would remain defensible if the people affected understood how it worked, whose objective it served, what evidence supported it, and how they could refuse, correct, or revise it.

## About the Author

::: {.author-profile-bio}
Huanren Warren Zhang is Associate Professor at [Aalborg University Business School](https://www.business.aau.dk/) and in the [Department of Economics at University of Southern Denmark](https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/institutter-centre/oekonomiskinstitut).

He is a behavioral economist who uses experiments, game theory, computational models, and empirical analysis to understand human and organizational behavior. His research examines strategic and risky decision-making, social norms, social preferences, social dilemmas, coordination, and human and organizational learning.
:::
::::
